```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Lake profile extrapolation function
LakeProfile <- function(dataset, variable, start_depth, end_depth, calc_interval, start_date, end_date) {
  
  # Description:
  
  #   This function generates data for lake profiles. It takes measurements as input and extrapolates in the given 
  #   interval values for the given time, depth, variable.
  
  # Inputs:
  
  #   dataset -> just give the name of the dataframe (type = dataframe)
  #   variable -> give the name of the variable of interest between ""(type = character) -> variable itself must be type integer/numerical
  #   stat_depth -> give the depth as an integer (type = int)
  #   end_depth -> give the depth as an integer (type = int)
  #   calc_interval -> give the extrapolation inverval as an integer (type = int)
  #   start_date -> give the date in the format "yyyy-mm-dd" (type = character)
  #   end_date -> give the date in the format "yyyy-mm-dd" (type = character)
  
  # Outputs: 
  
  #  Dataframe containing extrapolation for the chosen variable "variablename"
  
  innerfunction1 <- function(target_date, target_depth, dataset, variable) {
    data_for_date <- dataset %>% 
      filter(date == target_date) %>%
      arrange(depth)
    approx(data_for_date$depth, data_for_date[[variable]], xout = target_depth)$y
  }
  
  innerfunction2 <- function(target_depth, target_date, dataset, variable) {
    data_for_depth <- interp_depth %>% 
      filter(depth == target_depth) %>%
      arrange(date)
    data_for_depth$date <- as.Date(data_for_depth$date)
    approx(data_for_depth$date, data_for_depth[[variable]], xout = target_date)$y
  }
  
  interp_depth <- crossing(tibble(date = unique(dataset$date)), tibble(depth = seq(start_depth, end_depth, length.out = calc_interval))) %>% 
    group_by(date) %>% 
    mutate(!!variable := innerfunction1(date[1], depth, dataset, variable))
  
  raster <- crossing(tibble(date = seq(as.Date(start_date), as.Date(end_date), by = 1)), tibble(depth = unique(interp_depth$depth))) %>%
    group_by(depth) %>%
    mutate(!!variable := innerfunction2(depth[1], date, interp_depth, variable))
  
  return(raster)
}

#Function to Plot the Profiles
PlotProfiles_Flexible <- function(profile, variable, interval_legend_ticks, interval_contour_lines, plot_title, legend_title, color_palette) {
  
  # Description:
  
  #   This function generates lake profile plots using plotly
  
  # Inputs:
  
  #   profile -> dataset for the given lake profile (type = dataframe)
  #   variable -> variable for which the profile should be generated ""(type = character)
  #   interval_legend_ticks -> interval of the ticks in the legend (type = int)
  #   interval_legend_ticks -> at which interval should a contour line be drawn (type = int)
  #   plot_title -> give the title of the plot between "" (type = character)
  #   legend_title -> give the legend title between "" (type = character)
  #   color_palette -> give a desired color pallette from rcolorbrewer between "" (type = character)
  
  # Outputs: 
  
  #  Dataframe containing extrapolation for the chosen variable "variablename"
  
  #Set Plot Settings
  min_val <- min(profile[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE)
  max_val <- max(profile[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE)
  legend_ticks <- round(seq(min_val, max_val,by = interval_legend_ticks))
  
  #Plot
  plotly_plot <- plot_ly(x = profile$date,
        y = profile$depth,
        z = profile[[variable]],
        type = "contour",
        colors = color_palette,
        contours = list(
                 start = min_val,
                 end = max_val,
                 size = interval_contour_lines,
                 coloring = 'heatmap',
                 showlines = TRUE
               ),
        colorbar = list(
                 title = legend_title,
                 tickmode = "array",
                 tickvals = legend_ticks, 
                 ticktext = legend_ticks
               )) %>%
  layout(yaxis = list(autorange = "reversed", title = "Depth [m]")) %>%
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "Date")) %>%
  layout(title = list(text = plot_title)) %>%
  colorbar(title = legend_title)

  return(plotly_plot)
}

#Function to Plot the Profiles
PlotProfiles_Fixed <- function(profile, variable, plot_title, legend_title, color_palette) {
  
  # Description:
  
  #   This function generates lake profile plots using plotly
  
  # Inputs:
  
  #   profile -> dataset for the given lake profile (type = dataframe)
  #   variable -> variable for which the profile should be generated ""(type = character)
  #   plot_title -> give the title of the plot between "" (type = character)
  #   legend_title -> give the legend title between "" (type = character)
  #   color_palette -> give a desired color pallette from rcolorbrewer between "" (type = character)
  
  # Outputs: 
  
  #  Dataframe containing extrapolation for the chosen variable "variablename"
  
  #Plot
  plotly_plot <- plot_ly(x = profile$date,
        y = profile$depth,
        z = profile[[variable]],
        type = "contour",
        colors = color_palette) %>% 
  layout(yaxis = list(autorange = "reversed", title = "Depth [m]")) %>%
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "Date")) %>%
  layout(title = list(text = plot_title)) %>%
  colorbar(title = legend_title)

  return(plotly_plot)
}
```

### Sampling site and map of lake zurich
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Nature-style overview map of Lake Zurich sampling sites
#
# FEATURES
# --------
# - Shows two study locations:
#   1) LZ-BITS sampling site:
#      47°19′15.2″ N, 8°33′32.0″ E
#   2) Long term monitoring sampling site:
#      47°18′16″ N, 8°34′31″ E
# - Downloads Lake Zurich polygon from OpenStreetMap
# - Includes Zurich for orientation
# - Adds a north arrow
# - Uses the confirmed working Overpass endpoint:
#     https://lz4.overpass-api.de/api/interpreter
# - Clean, publication-style map appearance
#
# OUTPUT
# ------
# Lake_Zurich_two_sampling_sites.png
# ============================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf)
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(osmdata)
  library(rnaturalearth)
  library(rnaturalearthdata)
  library(ggspatial)
})

# ============================================================
# 1) Sampling locations
# ============================================================
# LZ-BITS sampling site
sample1_lat <- 47 + 19/60 + 15.2/3600
sample1_lon <- 8 + 33/60 + 32.0/3600

# Long term monitoring sampling site
sample2_lat <- 47 + 18/60 + 16/3600
sample2_lon <- 8 + 34/60 + 31/3600

sites_df <- data.frame(
  name = c("LZ-BITS sampling site", "Long term monitoring sampling site"),
  lon  = c(sample1_lon, sample2_lon),
  lat  = c(sample1_lat, sample2_lat),
  coord_label = c(
    "47°19′15.2″N, 8°33′32.0″E",
    "47°18′16″N, 8°34′31″E"
  ),
  fill_col = c("#c62828", "#7b1fa2")  # red, violet
)

sampling_sites <- st_as_sf(
  sites_df,
  coords = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs = 4326
)

site_xy <- st_coordinates(sampling_sites)

sites_plot_df <- sites_df |>
  mutate(
    x = site_xy[, 1],
    y = site_xy[, 2]
  )

# ============================================================
# 2) Download Lake Zurich polygon from OSM
# ============================================================
set_overpass_url("https://lz4.overpass-api.de/api/interpreter")

q <- opq(
  bbox = c(8.35, 47.10, 8.95, 47.45)
) |>
  add_osm_feature(key = "natural", value = "water")

osm <- osmdata_sf(q)

water_polys <- bind_rows(
  osm$osm_polygons,
  osm$osm_multipolygons
)

lake <- water_polys |>
  filter(!is.na(name)) |>
  filter(name %in% c("Zürichsee", "Zurichsee", "Lake Zurich"))

# Fallback if name-based match fails
if (nrow(lake) == 0) {
  message("Named Lake Zurich polygon not found; using largest water polygon in query area.")
  water_proj <- st_transform(water_polys, 2056)
  lake <- water_polys[which.max(st_area(water_proj)), ]
}

lake <- st_make_valid(lake)

# ============================================================
# 3) Get Zurich for orientation
# ============================================================
places <- ne_download(
  scale = 10,
  type = "populated_places",
  category = "cultural",
  returnclass = "sf"
)

bb <- st_bbox(lake)

cities <- places |>
  filter(
    LONGITUDE >= bb["xmin"] - 0.05,
    LONGITUDE <= bb["xmax"] + 0.05,
    LATITUDE  >= bb["ymin"] - 0.05,
    LATITUDE  <= bb["ymax"] + 0.05
  ) |>
  filter(NAME %in% c("Zurich", "Zürich"))

city_coords <- st_coordinates(cities)

cities_df <- cities |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(
    x = city_coords[, 1],
    y = city_coords[, 2]
  )

# ============================================================
# 4) Plot extent
# ============================================================
xpad <- 0.045
ypad_bottom <- 0.030
ypad_top <- 0.050

xmin <- bb["xmin"] - xpad
xmax <- bb["xmax"] + xpad
ymin <- bb["ymin"] - ypad_bottom
ymax <- bb["ymax"] + ypad_top

# ============================================================
# 5) Build Nature-like plot
# ============================================================
p <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = lake,
    fill = "#d9ecf5",
    color = "#6a8fa6",
    linewidth = 0.35
  ) +

  # LZ-BITS site (red)
  geom_sf(
    data = sampling_sites |> filter(name == "LZ-BITS sampling site"),
    shape = 21,
    size = 3.4,
    fill = "#c62828",
    color = "black",
    stroke = 0.25
  ) +

  # Long-term monitoring site (violet)
  geom_sf(
    data = sampling_sites |> filter(name == "Long term monitoring sampling site"),
    shape = 21,
    size = 3.4,
    fill = "#7b1fa2",
    color = "black",
    stroke = 0.25
  ) +

  # LZ-BITS label and coordinates above point
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = sites_plot_df$x[sites_plot_df$name == "LZ-BITS sampling site"],
    y = sites_plot_df$y[sites_plot_df$name == "LZ-BITS sampling site"] + 0.013,
    label = "LZ-BITS sampling site",
    hjust = 0.5,
    size = 3.6,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = sites_plot_df$x[sites_plot_df$name == "LZ-BITS sampling site"],
    y = sites_plot_df$y[sites_plot_df$name == "LZ-BITS sampling site"] + 0.006,
    label = "47°19′15.2″N, 8°33′32.0″E",
    hjust = 0.5,
    size = 3.0
  ) +

  # Long-term monitoring label and coordinates below point
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = sites_plot_df$x[sites_plot_df$name == "Long term monitoring sampling site"],
    y = sites_plot_df$y[sites_plot_df$name == "Long term monitoring sampling site"] - 0.010,
    label = "Long term monitoring sampling site",
    hjust = 0.5,
    size = 3.6,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = sites_plot_df$x[sites_plot_df$name == "Long term monitoring sampling site"],
    y = sites_plot_df$y[sites_plot_df$name == "Long term monitoring sampling site"] - 0.017,
    label = "47°18′16″N, 8°34′31″E",
    hjust = 0.5,
    size = 3.0
  ) +

  geom_sf(
    data = cities,
    color = "black",
    size = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = cities_df,
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = NAME),
    nudge_y = 0.008,
    size = 3.0
  ) +
  annotation_north_arrow(
    location = "tr",
    which_north = "true",
    pad_x = unit(0.25, "cm"),
    pad_y = unit(0.25, "cm"),
    style = north_arrow_fancy_orienteering(
      text_size = 7,
      line_width = 0.7
    )
  ) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(xmin, xmax),
    ylim = c(ymin, ymax),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
    plot.margin = margin(6, 6, 6, 6)
  )

print(p)

# ============================================================
# 6) Export as PNG
# ============================================================
ggsave(
  filename = "Lake_Zurich_two_sampling_sites.png",
  plot = p,
  width = 14,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)
```

```{r}
############################################################
# ST_Bacteria_Plot
#
# PURPOSE
# -------
# Reproduce bacterial abundance as a Spring Bloom 2021
# short-term (ST) lake profile in the same overall style
# as the ST plots in Sample_Overview.Rmd:
#   - profile interpolation in depth and time
#   - Plotly contour plot
#   - reversed depth axis
#   - restricted ST time window only
#
# INPUT REQUIRED
# --------------
# FC_FULL.csv with at least these columns:
#   - date
#   - depth
#   - bac_abu
#
# OUTPUT
# ------
# Interactive Plotly object + optional HTML export
############################################################

########################
## 0) Setup
########################
data_dir <- "/SynologyDrive/PhD/Projects/SpringBloom2021/DataAnalysis_SpringBloom2021/Supplementary/LakeProfiles/"
out_dir  <- data_dir

ST_START <- as.Date("2021-02-22")
ST_END   <- as.Date("2021-06-07")

# Same ST depth focus as the Sample_Overview ST profiles
ST_DEPTH_MIN <- 0
ST_DEPTH_MAX <- 40

########################
## 1) Libraries
########################
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(lubridate)
  library(plotly)
  library(htmlwidgets)
  library(RColorBrewer)
})

########################
## 2) Lake profile function
########################
# This follows the same logic as in Sample_Overview.Rmd:
# 1) interpolate across depth for each date
# 2) interpolate across time for each depth
LakeProfile <- function(dataset, variable, start_depth, end_depth,
                        calc_interval, start_date, end_date) {

  innerfunction1 <- function(target_date, target_depth, dataset, variable) {
    data_for_date <- dataset %>%
      filter(date == target_date) %>%
      arrange(depth)

    # Need at least 2 measurements for interpolation
    if (nrow(data_for_date) < 2) {
      return(rep(NA_real_, length(target_depth)))
    }

    approx(
      x = data_for_date$depth,
      y = data_for_date[[variable]],
      xout = target_depth,
      rule = 2
    )$y
  }

  interp_depth <- tidyr::crossing(
    tibble(date = unique(dataset$date)),
    tibble(depth = seq(start_depth, end_depth, length.out = calc_interval))
  ) %>%
    group_by(date) %>%
    mutate(!!variable := innerfunction1(date[1], depth, dataset, variable)) %>%
    ungroup()

  innerfunction2 <- function(target_depth, target_date, dataset, variable) {
    data_for_depth <- interp_depth %>%
      filter(depth == target_depth) %>%
      arrange(date)

    data_for_depth$date <- as.Date(data_for_depth$date)

    good <- !is.na(data_for_depth[[variable]])
    if (sum(good) < 2) {
      return(rep(NA_real_, length(target_date)))
    }

    approx(
      x = as.numeric(data_for_depth$date[good]),
      y = data_for_depth[[variable]][good],
      xout = as.numeric(target_date),
      rule = 2
    )$y
  }

  raster <- tidyr::crossing(
    tibble(date = seq(as.Date(start_date), as.Date(end_date), by = 1)),
    tibble(depth = unique(interp_depth$depth))
  ) %>%
    group_by(depth) %>%
    mutate(!!variable := innerfunction2(depth[1], date, interp_depth, variable)) %>%
    ungroup()

  return(raster)
}

########################
## 3) Plot function in ST style
########################
# Same general plotting logic as Sample_Overview.Rmd,
# but adapted for bacterial abundance.
PlotProfiles_Fixed <- function(profile, variable, plot_title, legend_title, color_palette) {

  plot_ly(
    x = profile$date,
    y = profile$depth,
    z = profile[[variable]],
    type = "contour",
    colors = color_palette
  ) %>%
    layout(
      title = list(text = plot_title),
      xaxis = list(title = "Date"),
      yaxis = list(
        autorange = "reversed",
        title = "Depth [m]"
      ),
      plot_bgcolor = "white"
    ) %>%
    colorbar(title = legend_title)
}

########################
## 4) Load and clean FC data
########################
fc_data <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(data_dir, "../../../Data/Lake_Data/Raw_Data/FC_FULL.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

fc_data_clean <- fc_data %>%
  mutate(
    date    = as.Date(date, format = "%m/%d/%Y"),
    depth   = as.numeric(depth),
    bac_abu = as.numeric(bac_abu)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(date),
    !is.na(depth),
    !is.na(bac_abu)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    date >= ST_START,
    date <= ST_END,
    depth >= ST_DEPTH_MIN,
    depth <= ST_DEPTH_MAX
  ) %>%
  arrange(date, depth)

########################
## 5) Build ST bacterial profile
########################
# Same interpolation density used for ST profiles in Sample_Overview
# (0-40 m, 1000 interpolated depth steps, daily interpolation in time)
bacteria_ST_profile <- LakeProfile(
  dataset       = fc_data_clean,
  variable      = "bac_abu",
  start_depth   = ST_DEPTH_MIN,
  end_depth     = ST_DEPTH_MAX,
  calc_interval = 1000,
  start_date    = ST_START,
  end_date      = ST_END
)

########################
## 6) Plot
########################
# Purple-pink palette chosen to stay visually close to your
# previous bacterial abundance plot, while keeping the ST contour style.
bac_palette_ST <- colorRampPalette(
  c("#f7fcf5", "#f2e5ff", "#d4b9da", "#c994c7",
    "#df65b0", "#e7298a", "#ce1256", "#980043", "#440154")
)(100)

ST_Bacteria_Plot <- PlotProfiles_Fixed(
  profile      = bacteria_ST_profile,
  variable     = "bac_abu",
  plot_title   = "Bacterial Abundance Profile",
  legend_title = "Bacteria [cells/mL]",
  color_palette = bac_palette_ST
)

ST_Bacteria_Plot

########################
## 7) Optional export
########################
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(
  ST_Bacteria_Plot,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "ST_Bacteria_Plot.html"),
  selfcontained = TRUE
)

########################
## 9) Export static image (recommended)
########################

# Make sure kaleido is available
# install.packages("reticulate")
# reticulate::py_install("kaleido")

export(ST_Bacteria_Plot,"ST_Bacteria_Plot.png")
```

```{r}
############################################################
# ENVIRONMENTAL CONTEXT AND TRANSPORTER ALLOCATION
#
# REQUIRED ALREADY-LOADED OBJECTS
# -------------------------------
# protein_final
# retained_species
# retained_species_dates
# abiotic_ST_dat
#
# ANALYSIS
# --------
# 1. Retain the authoritative species-date combinations.
# 2. Calculate species-date TPF using the original definition.
# 3. Calculate abundance-weighted pooled TPF overall and by
#    trophic strategy.
# 4. Calculate mean temperature and chlorophyll at 2–8 m.
# 5. Prepare one polished A4 landscape figure.
# 6. Export one tidy CSV containing all plotted values.
#
# IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
# ------------------------
# The figure describes transporter allocation across measured
# environmental variation. It does not identify an overturn
# period or demonstrate environmental causality.
############################################################


############################################################
# 0. LIBRARIES AND OUTPUT DIRECTORY
############################################################

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(stringr)
  library(readr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
})


############################################################
# 1. GLOBAL FIGURE SETTINGS
############################################################

# These values are used in every panel to ensure consistent
# line widths, point sizes and graphical weighting.

LINE_WIDTH   <- 0.75
POINT_SIZE   <- 1.45
RIBBON_ALPHA <- 0.20

BASE_SIZE   <- 8.5
AXIS_SIZE   <- 8.0
LEGEND_SIZE <- 7.8


trophic_colours <- c(
  "Oligotroph"   = "#99C3E6",
  "Intermediate" = "#ECEAE9",
  "Copiotroph"   = "#B25A3C"
)

environment_colours <- c(
  "Chlorophyll" = "#238B45",
  "Temperature" = "#C62828"
)

protein_class_colours <- c(
  "Non-transporter" = "#D9D9D9",
  "Transporter"     = "#5799C6"
)


############################################################
# 2. COMPACT PUBLICATION THEME
############################################################

theme_nature <- function(base_size = BASE_SIZE) {

  theme_classic(
    base_size = base_size,
    base_family = "sans"
  ) +

    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
        colour = "grey92",
        linewidth = 0.25
      ),

      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

      axis.line = element_line(
        colour = "black",
        linewidth = 0.35
      ),

      axis.ticks = element_line(
        colour = "black",
        linewidth = 0.30
      ),

      axis.ticks.length = grid::unit(
        1.4,
        "mm"
      ),

      axis.title = element_text(
        colour = "black",
        size = AXIS_SIZE
      ),

      axis.title.y = element_text(
        margin = margin(r = 3)
      ),

      axis.title.x = element_text(
        margin = margin(t = 3)
      ),

      axis.text = element_text(
        colour = "black",
        size = AXIS_SIZE - 0.3
      ),

      legend.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = LEGEND_SIZE
      ),

      legend.text = element_text(
        size = LEGEND_SIZE
      ),

      legend.key.height = grid::unit(
        3.4,
        "mm"
      ),

      legend.key.width = grid::unit(
        8,
        "mm"
      ),

      legend.spacing.x = grid::unit(
        1.5,
        "mm"
      ),

      legend.spacing.y = grid::unit(
        0,
        "mm"
      ),

      plot.margin = margin(
        t = 1.4,
        r = 4,
        b = 1.4,
        l = 4,
        unit = "mm"
      )
    )
}


############################################################
# 3. RECODE TROPHIC-STRATEGY LABELS
############################################################

recode_trophic_group <- function(x) {

  recoded_group <- dplyr::case_when(
    x == "Oligo_like"   ~ "Oligotroph",
    x == "Intermediate" ~ "Intermediate",
    x == "Copio_like"   ~ "Copiotroph",
    TRUE                ~ NA_character_
  )

  factor(
    recoded_group,
    levels = c(
      "Oligotroph",
      "Intermediate",
      "Copiotroph"
    )
  )
}


############################################################
# 4. PREPARE DATE COLUMNS
############################################################

protein_final <- protein_final %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Date = as.Date(Date)
  )

retained_species_dates <- retained_species_dates %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Date = as.Date(Date)
  )

abiotic_ST_dat <- abiotic_ST_dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    date = as.Date(date),
    depth = as.numeric(depth),
    temperature = as.numeric(temperature),
    chlorophyll = as.numeric(chlorophyll)
  )


############################################################
# 5. DEFINE THE AUTHORITATIVE RETAINED DATASET
############################################################

# Only the previously retained species and retained species-date
# combinations are included. No new occurrence filter is added.

retained_keys <- retained_species_dates %>%
  dplyr::semi_join(
    retained_species,
    by = c(
      "Species_ID",
      "Group_For_Plots"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    Species_ID,
    Date,
    Group_For_Plots
  )


############################################################
# 6. CLASSIFY TRANSPORTER PROTEINS
############################################################

retained_protein <- protein_final %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(
    retained_keys,
    by = c(
      "Species_ID",
      "Date",
      "Group_For_Plots"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Exact transporter definition used in the original
    # transporter-investment analysis.
    is_transporter =
      !is.na(KEGG_Subcategory) &
      stringr::str_detect(
        KEGG_Subcategory,
        "\\bTransporters\\b"
      ),

    # Exact normalized abundance measure.
    Protein_Abundance =
      Protein_Abundance_IBAQ_Norm,

    TrophicGroupPlot =
      recode_trophic_group(
        Group_For_Plots
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(TrophicGroupPlot),
    is.finite(Protein_Abundance)
  )


############################################################
# 7. CALCULATE SPECIES × DATE TPF
############################################################

# For each species and retained sampling date:
#
#       summed transporter protein abundance
# TPF = -------------------------------------
#       summed total protein abundance

species_date_tpf <- retained_protein %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Species_ID,
    Date,
    Group_For_Plots,
    TrophicGroupPlot
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Total_Protein_Abundance = sum(
      Protein_Abundance,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Transporter_Abundance = sum(
      Protein_Abundance[is_transporter],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Total_Protein_Abundance > 0
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    TPF =
      Transporter_Abundance /
      Total_Protein_Abundance,

    TPF_Percent =
      100 * TPF
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    TrophicGroupPlot,
    Species_ID,
    Date
  )


############################################################
# 8. CALCULATE OVERALL POOLED TPF
############################################################

# Abundances are summed before calculating TPF. Therefore,
# this is an abundance-weighted pooled fraction and not the
# arithmetic mean of species-level TPF values.

overall_date_tpf <- retained_protein %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Date
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Total_Protein_Abundance = sum(
      Protein_Abundance,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Transporter_Abundance = sum(
      Protein_Abundance[is_transporter],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    N_Contributing_Species = dplyr::n_distinct(
      Species_ID
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Total_Protein_Abundance > 0
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Pooled_TPF_Percent =
      100 *
      Transporter_Abundance /
      Total_Protein_Abundance,

    Non_Transporter_Percent =
      100 - Pooled_TPF_Percent
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    Date
  )


############################################################
# 9. CALCULATE POOLED TPF BY TROPHIC STRATEGY
############################################################

group_date_tpf <- retained_protein %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Date,
    TrophicGroupPlot
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Total_Protein_Abundance = sum(
      Protein_Abundance,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Transporter_Abundance = sum(
      Protein_Abundance[is_transporter],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    N_Contributing_Species = dplyr::n_distinct(
      Species_ID
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Total_Protein_Abundance > 0
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Pooled_TPF_Percent =
      100 *
      Transporter_Abundance /
      Total_Protein_Abundance
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    TrophicGroupPlot,
    Date
  )


############################################################
# 10. SPECIES-LEVEL TPF DISTRIBUTION
############################################################

# The interquartile range represents variation among species
# belonging to each strategy. It is not a confidence interval
# around the pooled TPF.

species_tpf_distribution <- species_date_tpf %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Date,
    TrophicGroupPlot
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    TPF_Q1 = stats::quantile(
      TPF_Percent,
      probs = 0.25,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    TPF_Q3 = stats::quantile(
      TPF_Percent,
      probs = 0.75,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

group_date_tpf <- group_date_tpf %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    species_tpf_distribution,
    by = c(
      "Date",
      "TrophicGroupPlot"
    )
  )


############################################################
# 11. CALCULATE MEAN ENVIRONMENTAL VALUES AT 2–8 M
############################################################

# These values are means of the available abiotic measurements
# collected between 2 and 8 m on each environmental sampling
# date. No temporal interpolation is performed here.

environment_2_8m <- abiotic_ST_dat %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    depth >= 2,
    depth <= 8
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Date = date
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Temperature = mean(
      temperature,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Chlorophyll = mean(
      chlorophyll,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    is.finite(Temperature),
    is.finite(Chlorophyll)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    Date
  )


############################################################
# 12. DEFINE THE COMMON FIGURE DATE RANGE
############################################################

figure_date_limits <- range(
  overall_date_tpf$Date,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

environment_2_8m <- environment_2_8m %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Date >= figure_date_limits[1],
    Date <= figure_date_limits[2]
  )


common_date_scale <- function() {

  scale_x_date(
    limits = figure_date_limits,
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b",
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  )
}


############################################################
# 13. PREPARE TROPHIC-STRATEGY LEGEND LABELS
############################################################

strategy_breaks <- c(
  "Oligotroph",
  "Intermediate",
  "Copiotroph"
)

strategy_counts <- retained_species %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Species_ID,

    TrophicGroupPlot =
      recode_trophic_group(
        Group_For_Plots
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(TrophicGroupPlot)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    Species_ID,
    TrophicGroupPlot
  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(
    TrophicGroupPlot,
    name = "Total_Retained_Species"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    TrophicGroupPlot
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Legend_Label = paste0(
      as.character(TrophicGroupPlot),
      " (n = ",
      Total_Retained_Species,
      ")"
    )
  )

strategy_legend_labels <- stats::setNames(
  strategy_counts$Legend_Label,
  as.character(strategy_counts$TrophicGroupPlot)
)


############################################################
# 14. PREPARE THE SECONDARY ENVIRONMENTAL AXIS
############################################################

# Temperature is mapped linearly onto the chlorophyll scale.
# The right y-axis reverses the transformation and displays
# temperature in its original units.

chlorophyll_min <- min(
  environment_2_8m$Chlorophyll,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

chlorophyll_max <- max(
  environment_2_8m$Chlorophyll,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

temperature_min <- min(
  environment_2_8m$Temperature,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

temperature_max <- max(
  environment_2_8m$Temperature,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

temperature_scale_factor <- (
  chlorophyll_max - chlorophyll_min
) / (
  temperature_max - temperature_min
)

temperature_offset <-
  chlorophyll_min -
  temperature_min * temperature_scale_factor

environment_2_8m <- environment_2_8m %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Temperature_Scaled =
      Temperature *
      temperature_scale_factor +
      temperature_offset
  )


############################################################
# 15. BUILD ONE DATASET CONTAINING ALL PLOTTED VALUES
############################################################

# Original_Value contains the interpretable measurement.
# Plot_Value contains the exact value passed to ggplot.
#
# These differ only for temperature because the secondary
# y-axis requires a linear transformation.

panel_a_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(

  environment_2_8m %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Panel = "A_Environment",
      Date,
      Series = "Chlorophyll",
      Original_Value = Chlorophyll,
      Plot_Value = Chlorophyll,
      Lower_Value = NA_real_,
      Upper_Value = NA_real_,
      Unit = "µg/L",
      Total_Retained_Species = NA_integer_,
      Axis_Scale_Factor = 1,
      Axis_Offset = 0
    ),

  environment_2_8m %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Panel = "A_Environment",
      Date,
      Series = "Temperature",
      Original_Value = Temperature,
      Plot_Value = Temperature_Scaled,
      Lower_Value = NA_real_,
      Upper_Value = NA_real_,
      Unit = "°C",
      Total_Retained_Species = NA_integer_,
      Axis_Scale_Factor =
        temperature_scale_factor,
      Axis_Offset =
        temperature_offset
    )
)


panel_b_data <- overall_date_tpf %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Date,
    Pooled_TPF_Percent,
    Non_Transporter_Percent
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      Pooled_TPF_Percent,
      Non_Transporter_Percent
    ),
    names_to = "Series",
    values_to = "Original_Value"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Series = dplyr::recode(
      Series,
      Pooled_TPF_Percent =
        "Transporter",
      Non_Transporter_Percent =
        "Non-transporter"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Panel = "B_Overall_Allocation",
    Date,
    Series,
    Original_Value,
    Plot_Value = Original_Value,
    Lower_Value = NA_real_,
    Upper_Value = NA_real_,
    Unit = "%",
    Total_Retained_Species = NA_integer_,
    Axis_Scale_Factor = NA_real_,
    Axis_Offset = NA_real_
  )


panel_c_data <- group_date_tpf %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    strategy_counts %>%
      dplyr::select(
        TrophicGroupPlot,
        Total_Retained_Species
      ),
    by = "TrophicGroupPlot"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Panel = "C_Strategy_TPF",
    Date,
    Series = as.character(
      TrophicGroupPlot
    ),
    Original_Value = Pooled_TPF_Percent,
    Plot_Value = Pooled_TPF_Percent,
    Lower_Value = TPF_Q1,
    Upper_Value = TPF_Q3,
    Unit = "%",
    Total_Retained_Species,
    Axis_Scale_Factor = NA_real_,
    Axis_Offset = NA_real_
  )


panel_d_data <- group_date_tpf %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    strategy_counts %>%
      dplyr::select(
        TrophicGroupPlot,
        Total_Retained_Species
      ),
    by = "TrophicGroupPlot"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Panel = "D_Contributing_Species",
    Date,
    Series = as.character(
      TrophicGroupPlot
    ),
    Original_Value = as.numeric(
      N_Contributing_Species
    ),
    Plot_Value = as.numeric(
      N_Contributing_Species
    ),
    Lower_Value = NA_real_,
    Upper_Value = NA_real_,
    Unit = "species",
    Total_Retained_Species,
    Axis_Scale_Factor = NA_real_,
    Axis_Offset = NA_real_
  )


plot_data_export <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  panel_a_data,
  panel_b_data,
  panel_c_data,
  panel_d_data
) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    Panel,
    Series,
    Date
  )


############################################################
# 16. EXPORT THE SINGLE PLOTTING DATAFILE
############################################################

readr::write_csv(
  plot_data_export,
  file.path(
    "SupplFig_Environmental_TPF_PlotData.csv"
  ),
  na = ""
)


############################################################
# 17. PANEL A: CHLOROPHYLL AND TEMPERATURE
############################################################

panel_a_plot_data <- plot_data_export %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Panel == "A_Environment"
  )


Environmental_Plot <- ggplot(
  panel_a_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = Date,
    y = Plot_Value,
    colour = Series,
    group = Series
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = LINE_WIDTH
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = POINT_SIZE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = "Environmental parameter",

    values = environment_colours,

    breaks = c(
      "Chlorophyll",
      "Temperature"
    ),

    labels = c(
      "Chlorophyll (mean 2–8 m depth)",
      "Temperature (mean 2–8 m depth)"
    ),

    guide = guide_legend(
      order = 1,
      nrow = 1,
      byrow = TRUE,
      title.position = "left"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Chlorophyll (µg/L)",

    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      trans = ~ (
        . - temperature_offset
      ) / temperature_scale_factor,

      name = "Temperature (°C)"
    ),

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0.05, 0.05)
    )
  ) +
  common_date_scale() +
  labs(
    x = NULL
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(
      colour = environment_colours["Chlorophyll"],
      face = "bold"
    ),

    axis.text.y.left = element_text(
      colour = environment_colours["Chlorophyll"]
    ),

    axis.title.y.right = element_text(
      colour = environment_colours["Temperature"],
      face = "bold",
      margin = margin(l = 3)
    ),

    axis.text.y.right = element_text(
      colour = environment_colours["Temperature"]
    ),

    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )


############################################################
# 18. PANEL B: OVERALL PROTEOME ALLOCATION
############################################################

panel_b_plot_data <- plot_data_export %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Panel == "B_Overall_Allocation"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Series = factor(
      Series,
      levels = c(
        "Non-transporter",
        "Transporter"
      )
    )
  )


Overall_Allocation_Plot <- ggplot(
  panel_b_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = Date,
    y = Plot_Value,
    fill = Series
  )
) +
  geom_area(
    position = "stack",
    alpha = 1
  ) +

  # Add the transporter boundary using the same graphical
  # dimensions as the other time-series panels.
  geom_line(
    data = panel_b_plot_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        Series == "Transporter"
      ),
    aes(
      x = Date,
      y = Plot_Value,
      group = 1
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = protein_class_colours["Transporter"],
    linewidth = LINE_WIDTH
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = panel_b_plot_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        Series == "Transporter"
      ),
    aes(
      x = Date,
      y = Plot_Value
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = protein_class_colours["Transporter"],
    size = POINT_SIZE
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Protein class",
    values = protein_class_colours,
    drop = FALSE,

    guide = guide_legend(
      order = 2,
      nrow = 1,
      byrow = TRUE,
      title.position = "left"
    )
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +

  common_date_scale() +

  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Community proteome\nallocation (%)"
  ) +

  theme_nature() +

  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )


############################################################
# 19. PANEL C: TPF BY TROPHIC STRATEGY
############################################################

panel_c_plot_data <- plot_data_export %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Panel == "C_Strategy_TPF"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Series = factor(
      Series,
      levels = strategy_breaks
    )
  )


Strategy_TPF_Plot <- ggplot(
  panel_c_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = Date,
    y = Plot_Value,
    colour = Series,
    group = Series
  )
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = Lower_Value,
      ymax = Upper_Value,
      fill = Series
    ),
    alpha = RIBBON_ALPHA,
    colour = NA,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = LINE_WIDTH
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = POINT_SIZE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = "Trophic strategy",
    values = trophic_colours,
    breaks = strategy_breaks,

    labels = strategy_legend_labels[
      strategy_breaks
    ],

    drop = FALSE,

    guide = guide_legend(
      order = 3,
      nrow = 1,
      byrow = TRUE,
      title.position = "left",

      override.aes = list(
        linewidth = LINE_WIDTH,
        size = POINT_SIZE
      )
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = trophic_colours,
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.01))
  ) +
  common_date_scale() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Pooled transporter\nproteome fraction (%)"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )


############################################################
# 20. PANEL D: CONTRIBUTING SPECIES
############################################################

panel_d_plot_data <- plot_data_export %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Panel == "D_Contributing_Species"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Series = factor(
      Series,
      levels = strategy_breaks
    )
  )


Contributor_Plot <- ggplot(
  panel_d_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = Date,
    y = Plot_Value,
    colour = Series,
    group = Series
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = LINE_WIDTH,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = POINT_SIZE,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = trophic_colours
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.05)
    )
  ) +
  common_date_scale() +
  labs(
    x = "Date",
    y = "Detected contributing\nspecies"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none"
  )


############################################################
# 21. COMBINE PANELS AND COLLECT LEGENDS
############################################################

Environmental_TPF_Figure <- (

  (
    Environmental_Plot /
      Overall_Allocation_Plot /
      Strategy_TPF_Plot /
      Contributor_Plot
  ) +

    patchwork::plot_layout(
      heights = c(
        0.85,
        0.80,
        1.05,
        0.65
      ),

      guides = "collect"
    ) +

    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      tag_levels = "A",

      theme = theme(
        plot.tag = element_text(
          face = "bold",
          size = 10
        )
      )
    )

) &

  theme(
    # Each legend group is given its own compact row below
    # the figure, preventing cropped legend entries.
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.justification = "center",
    legend.box.just = "center",

    legend.box.spacing = grid::unit(
      0.5,
      "mm"
    ),

    legend.box.margin = margin(
      t = 1,
      r = 0,
      b = 0,
      l = 0,
      unit = "mm"
    )
  )


############################################################
# 22. DISPLAY AND EXPORT THE FINAL FIGURE
############################################################

Environmental_TPF_Figure


# Exact A4 landscape dimensions:
#
# Width  = 297 mm
# Height = 210 mm

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    "SupplFig_Environmental_TPF_A4_Landscape.pdf"
  ),
  plot = Environmental_TPF_Figure,
  width = 297,
  height = 210,
  units = "mm",
  bg = "white"
)

ggsave(

    "SupplFig_Environmental_TPF_A4_Landscape.png"
  ),
  plot = Environmental_TPF_Figure,
  width = 297,
  height = 210,

  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)
```

```{r}
############################################################
# ENVIRONMENTAL CONTEXT AND RHODOPSIN PROTEOME ALLOCATION
# WHOLE-DATASET VERSION USED FOR FIGURE 5
#
# A) Mean measured light and temperature at 2–8 m
# B) Community rhodopsin proteome fraction
# C) Pooled rhodopsin fraction: Oligotroph versus Other
# D) Species with detected rhodopsin protein per date
#
# Rhodopsin KOs: K04641 and K04643
# Protein detection: normalized iBAQ > 0
# Environmental values: measured 2–8 m means; no interpolation
############################################################


############################################################
# 0. LIBRARIES AND INPUT PATHS
############################################################

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(stringr)
  library(readr)
  library(readxl)
  library(lubridate)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
})

# Run from the directory containing Sample_Overview.Rmd.
protein_path <- "../../Figure_03/LakeOverview/Species_Protein_Table.csv"
species_path <- "../../Figure_03/LakeOverview/Species_Meta_Table.csv"
gene_path    <- "../../Figure_03/LakeOverview/Species_Gene_Table.csv"
abiotic_path <- "../../../Data/Lake_Data/Raw_Data/Data_2021.xlsx"
light_path <- "../../../Data/Lake_Data/Raw_Data/Light_Measurements_2021.xlsx"

############################################################
# 1. LOAD DATA
############################################################

protein_table <- read_csv(
  protein_path,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

species_meta <- read_csv(
  species_path,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

gene_table <- read_csv(
  gene_path,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

abiotic_ST_dat <- read_excel(
  abiotic_path,
  sheet = "abiotic"
)

light_raw <- read_excel(light_path)


############################################################
# 2. VALIDATE REQUIRED COLUMNS
############################################################

check_columns <- function(data, required, object_name) {

  missing_columns <- setdiff(
    required,
    names(data)
  )

  if (length(missing_columns) > 0L) {
    stop(
      object_name,
      " is missing: ",
      paste(
        missing_columns,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  }
}

check_columns(
  protein_table,
  c(
    "Date",
    "Species_ID",
    "Protein_ID",
    "Protein_Abundance_IBAQ_Norm"
  ),
  "Species_Protein_Table.csv"
)

check_columns(
  species_meta,
  c(
    "Species_ID",
    "Group_For_Plots"
  ),
  "Species_Meta_Table.csv"
)

check_columns(
  gene_table,
  c(
    "Species_ID",
    "Protein_ID",
    "KEGG_ID"
  ),
  "Species_Gene_Table.csv"
)

check_columns(
  abiotic_ST_dat,
  c(
    "date",
    "depth",
    "temperature"
  ),
  "Data_2021.xlsx: abiotic"
)

check_columns(
  light_raw,
  c(
    "Day",
    "Depth",
    "Licht_spher"
  ),
  "Light_Measurements_2021 workbook"
)


############################################################
# 3. HELPERS AND FIGURE SETTINGS
############################################################

parse_mixed_date <- function(x) {

  if (inherits(x, "Date")) {
    return(x)
  }

  if (inherits(x, c("POSIXct", "POSIXt"))) {
    return(as.Date(x))
  }

  if (is.numeric(x)) {
    return(
      as.Date(
        x,
        origin = "1899-12-30"
      )
    )
  }

  as.Date(
    parse_date_time(
      as.character(x),
      orders = c(
        "ymd",
        "mdy",
        "dmy"
      ),
      quiet = TRUE
    )
  )
}


# Figure 5 compares oligotroph-like taxa with all remaining taxa.
#
# This preserves all 495 species instead of silently discarding
# taxa whose three-class trophic assignment was filtered.
recode_figure5_group <- function(x) {

  factor(
    if_else(
      x == "Oligo_like",
      "Oligotroph",
      "Other",
      missing = "Other"
    ),
    levels = c(
      "Oligotroph",
      "Other"
    )
  )
}


theme_nature <- function(base_size = 8.5) {

  theme_classic(
    base_size = base_size,
    base_family = "sans"
  ) +
    theme(
      axis.title = element_text(
        colour = "black"
      ),

      axis.text = element_text(
        colour = "black"
      ),

      axis.line = element_line(
        linewidth = 0.4,
        colour = "black"
      ),

      axis.ticks = element_line(
        linewidth = 0.35,
        colour = "black"
      ),

      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
        linewidth = 0.25,
        colour = "#E7E7E7"
      ),

      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

      plot.margin = margin(
        4, 5, 4, 5
      ),

      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.box = "vertical",

      legend.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 7.8
      ),

      legend.text = element_text(
        size = 7.8
      ),

      plot.tag = element_text(
        size = 11,
        face = "plain"
      )
    )
}


group_colours <- c(
  "Oligotroph" = "#99C3E6",
  "Other"      = "#777777"
)

environment_colours <- c(
  "Light"       = "#D69F00",
  "Temperature" = "#C62828"
)

rhodopsin_colour <- "#8E5AA9"

LINE_WIDTH <- 0.75
POINT_SIZE <- 1.45

rhodo_kos <- c(
  "K04641",
  "K04643"
)


############################################################
# 4. BUILD A UNIQUE RHODOPSIN ANNOTATION MAP
############################################################

# Collapse the gene table to exactly one row for every
# Species_ID × Protein_ID.
#
# This prevents abundance rows from being duplicated if the
# gene table contains multiple annotation rows for a protein.
protein_rhodopsin_map <- gene_table %>%
  transmute(
    Species_ID,
    Protein_ID,

    is_rhodopsin = str_detect(
      coalesce(
        as.character(KEGG_ID),
        ""
      ),
      "\\b(K04641|K04643)\\b"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    Species_ID,
    Protein_ID
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    is_rhodopsin =
      any(is_rhodopsin),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


# Gene carriers are used only as a genomic QC count.
rhodopsin_gene_species <- protein_rhodopsin_map %>%
  filter(is_rhodopsin) %>%
  distinct(Species_ID)


############################################################
# 5. ANNOTATE THE COMPLETE PROTEIN TABLE
############################################################

species_group_map <- species_meta %>%
  transmute(
    Species_ID,

    Figure5_Group =
      recode_figure5_group(
        Group_For_Plots
      )
  ) %>%
  distinct()


protein_analysis <- protein_table %>%
  mutate(
    Date = parse_mixed_date(Date)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    protein_rhodopsin_map,
    by = c(
      "Species_ID",
      "Protein_ID"
    )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    species_group_map,
    by = "Species_ID"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    is_rhodopsin =
      coalesce(
        is_rhodopsin,
        FALSE
      ),

    Protein_Abundance =
      as.numeric(
        Protein_Abundance_IBAQ_Norm
      )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Date),
    !is.na(Figure5_Group),
    is.finite(Protein_Abundance),

    # Positive normalized iBAQ defines protein detection.
    Protein_Abundance > 0
  )


# A detected rhodopsin therefore requires:
#
# 1. K04641 or K04643 in the gene annotation;
# 2. a matching Protein_ID in the protein table;
# 3. normalized iBAQ greater than zero.
rhodopsin_detected_species <- protein_analysis %>%
  filter(is_rhodopsin) %>%
  distinct(
    Species_ID,
    Figure5_Group
  )


############################################################
# 6. SPECIES-DATE RHODOPSIN PROTEOME FRACTION
############################################################

# All detected proteins remain in the denominator.
#
# Species without detected rhodopsin on a date receive:
# Rhodopsin_Abundance = 0
# RPF_Percent = 0
species_date_rpf <- protein_analysis %>%
  group_by(
    Species_ID,
    Date,
    Figure5_Group
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Protein_Abundance = sum(
      Protein_Abundance,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Rhodopsin_Abundance = sum(
      Protein_Abundance[is_rhodopsin],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    Total_Protein_Abundance > 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    RPF =
      Rhodopsin_Abundance /
      Total_Protein_Abundance,

    RPF_Percent =
      100 * RPF
  )


############################################################
# 7. COMMUNITY-WIDE RHODOPSIN FRACTION
############################################################

# Abundances are summed before division.
#
# This is a pooled community fraction, not the arithmetic
# mean of individual species fractions.
overall_date_rpf <- protein_analysis %>%
  group_by(Date) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Protein_Abundance = sum(
      Protein_Abundance,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Rhodopsin_Abundance = sum(
      Protein_Abundance[is_rhodopsin],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    Total_Protein_Abundance > 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Rhodopsin_Percent =
      100 *
      Rhodopsin_Abundance /
      Total_Protein_Abundance
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date)


############################################################
# 8. RHODOPSIN FRACTION BY FIGURE 5 GROUP
############################################################

# Abundances are summed before division within each group.
#
# These are pooled, abundance-weighted group fractions.
group_date_rpf <- protein_analysis %>%
  group_by(
    Date,
    Figure5_Group
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Protein_Abundance = sum(
      Protein_Abundance,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Rhodopsin_Abundance = sum(
      Protein_Abundance[is_rhodopsin],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    Total_Protein_Abundance > 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Pooled_RPF_Percent =
      100 *
      Rhodopsin_Abundance /
      Total_Protein_Abundance
  )


############################################################
# 9. DATE-SPECIFIC RHODOPSIN-PROTEIN CONTRIBUTORS
############################################################

# Count only species with positive detected rhodopsin
# abundance on each date.
rhodopsin_contributor_counts <- species_date_rpf %>%
  filter(
    Rhodopsin_Abundance > 0
  ) %>%
  count(
    Date,
    Figure5_Group,
    name = "N_Rhodopsin_Species"
  )


# Explicitly represent date × group combinations without
# detected rhodopsin as zero.
rhodopsin_contributors <- group_date_rpf %>%
  distinct(
    Date,
    Figure5_Group
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    rhodopsin_contributor_counts,
    by = c(
      "Date",
      "Figure5_Group"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    N_Rhodopsin_Species =
      coalesce(
        N_Rhodopsin_Species,
        0L
      )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    Figure5_Group,
    Date
  )


# Include the count in the group-level exported table.
group_date_rpf <- group_date_rpf %>%
  left_join(
    rhodopsin_contributors,
    by = c(
      "Date",
      "Figure5_Group"
    )
  )


############################################################
# 10. MEAN MEASURED LIGHT AND TEMPERATURE AT 2–8 M
############################################################

light_clean <- light_raw %>%
  transmute(
    Date =
      parse_mixed_date(Day),

    depth =
      as.numeric(Depth),

    Light =
      as.numeric(Licht_spher)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Date),
    is.finite(depth),
    is.finite(Light)
  )


temperature_clean <- abiotic_ST_dat %>%
  transmute(
    Date =
      parse_mixed_date(date),

    depth =
      as.numeric(depth),

    Temperature =
      as.numeric(temperature)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Date),
    is.finite(depth),
    is.finite(Temperature)
  )


light_2_8m <- light_clean %>%
  filter(
    depth >= 2,
    depth <= 8
  ) %>%
  group_by(Date) %>%
  summarise(
    Light = mean(
      Light,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    N_Light_Depths =
      n_distinct(depth),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


temperature_2_8m <- temperature_clean %>%
  filter(
    depth >= 2,
    depth <= 8
  ) %>%
  group_by(Date) %>%
  summarise(
    Temperature = mean(
      Temperature,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    N_Temperature_Depths =
      n_distinct(depth),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


# Retain only dates measured for both light and temperature.
#
# No temporal interpolation or missing-date filling is used.
environment_2_8m <- inner_join(
  light_2_8m,
  temperature_2_8m,
  by = "Date"
) %>%
  arrange(Date)


figure_date_limits <- range(
  overall_date_rpf$Date,
  na.rm = TRUE
)


environment_2_8m <- environment_2_8m %>%
  filter(
    Date >= figure_date_limits[[1]],
    Date <= figure_date_limits[[2]]
  )


if (nrow(environment_2_8m) == 0L) {
  stop(
    "No common 2–8 m light and temperature dates ",
    "occur in the proteomic time window."
  )
}


############################################################
# 11. PREPARE DUAL ENVIRONMENTAL AXIS
############################################################

light_range <- range(
  environment_2_8m$Light,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

temperature_range <- range(
  environment_2_8m$Temperature,
  na.rm = TRUE
)


if (
  diff(light_range) == 0 ||
  diff(temperature_range) == 0
) {
  stop(
    "Light and temperature must each contain ",
    "at least two distinct values."
  )
}


temperature_scale_factor <-
  diff(light_range) /
  diff(temperature_range)


temperature_offset <-
  light_range[[1]] -
  temperature_range[[1]] *
  temperature_scale_factor


environment_2_8m <- environment_2_8m %>%
  mutate(
    Temperature_Scaled =
      Temperature *
      temperature_scale_factor +
      temperature_offset
  )


common_date_scale <- function() {

  scale_x_date(
    limits = figure_date_limits,
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b",
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0)
    )
  )
}


############################################################
# 12. LEGEND LABELS
############################################################

group_breaks <- c(
  "Oligotroph",
  "Other"
)


# These counts should reproduce the Figure 5 values:
# Oligotroph = 20
# Other      = 27
rhodopsin_group_counts <- rhodopsin_detected_species %>%
  count(
    Figure5_Group,
    name = "N_Rhodopsin_Species"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Legend_Label = paste0(
      Figure5_Group,
      " (rhodopsin n = ",
      N_Rhodopsin_Species,
      ")"
    )
  )


group_legend_labels <- setNames(
  rhodopsin_group_counts$Legend_Label,
  as.character(
    rhodopsin_group_counts$Figure5_Group
  )
)


############################################################
# 13. PANEL A: LIGHT AND TEMPERATURE
############################################################

panel_a_long <- bind_rows(

  environment_2_8m %>%
    transmute(
      Date,
      Series = "Light",
      Original_Value = Light,
      Plot_Value = Light,
      N_Depths = N_Light_Depths
    ),

  environment_2_8m %>%
    transmute(
      Date,
      Series = "Temperature",
      Original_Value = Temperature,
      Plot_Value = Temperature_Scaled,
      N_Depths = N_Temperature_Depths
    )
)


Environmental_Plot <- ggplot(
  panel_a_long,
  aes(
    x = Date,
    y = Plot_Value,
    colour = Series,
    group = Series
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = LINE_WIDTH
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = POINT_SIZE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = "Environmental parameter",

    values = environment_colours,

    breaks = c(
      "Light",
      "Temperature"
    ),

    labels = c(
      "Light (mean 2–8 m depth)",
      "Temperature (mean 2–8 m depth)"
    ),

    guide = guide_legend(
      order = 1,
      nrow = 1,
      byrow = TRUE,
      title.position = "left"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    # Change this label if Licht_spher uses another unit.
    name = "Spherical light (µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹)",

    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      trans = ~ (
        . - temperature_offset
      ) / temperature_scale_factor,

      name = "Temperature (°C)"
    ),

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0.05, 0.05)
    )
  ) +
  common_date_scale() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    tag = "A"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(
      colour =
        environment_colours[["Light"]],
      face = "bold"
    ),

    axis.text.y.left = element_text(
      colour =
        environment_colours[["Light"]]
    ),

    axis.title.y.right = element_text(
      colour =
        environment_colours[["Temperature"]],
      face = "bold"
    ),

    axis.text.y.right = element_text(
      colour =
        environment_colours[["Temperature"]]
    ),

    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )


############################################################
# 14. PANEL B: COMMUNITY RHODOPSIN FRACTION
############################################################

overall_y_max <- max(
  overall_date_rpf$Rhodopsin_Percent,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

if (
  !is.finite(overall_y_max) ||
  overall_y_max <= 0
) {
  overall_y_max <- 1
}


Overall_RPF_Plot <- ggplot(
  overall_date_rpf,
  aes(
    x = Date,
    y = Rhodopsin_Percent
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    colour = rhodopsin_colour,
    linewidth = LINE_WIDTH
  ) +
  geom_point(
    colour = rhodopsin_colour,
    size = POINT_SIZE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      0,
      1.08 * overall_y_max
    ),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0)
    )
  ) +
  common_date_scale() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Community rhodopsin\nproteome fraction (%)",
    tag = "B"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )


############################################################
# 15. PANEL C: RHODOPSIN FRACTION BY FIGURE 5 GROUP
############################################################

# No species-level IQR ribbons are plotted because those
# quartiles are not uncertainty intervals around these pooled
# abundance-weighted curves.
group_y_max <- max(
  group_date_rpf$Pooled_RPF_Percent,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

if (
  !is.finite(group_y_max) ||
  group_y_max <= 0
) {
  group_y_max <- 1
}


Strategy_RPF_Plot <- ggplot(
  group_date_rpf,
  aes(
    x = Date,
    y = Pooled_RPF_Percent,
    colour = Figure5_Group,
    group = Figure5_Group
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = LINE_WIDTH
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = POINT_SIZE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = "Figure 5 group",

    values = group_colours,
    breaks = group_breaks,

    labels =
      group_legend_labels[
        group_breaks
      ],

    drop = FALSE,

    guide = guide_legend(
      order = 2,
      nrow = 1,
      byrow = TRUE,
      title.position = "left"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      0,
      1.08 * group_y_max
    ),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0)
    )
  ) +
  common_date_scale() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Pooled rhodopsin\nproteome fraction (%)",
    tag = "C"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )


############################################################
# 16. PANEL D: SPECIES WITH DETECTED RHODOPSIN PROTEIN
############################################################

Contributor_Plot <- ggplot(
  rhodopsin_contributors,
  aes(
    x = Date,
    y = N_Rhodopsin_Species,
    colour = Figure5_Group,
    group = Figure5_Group
  )
) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = LINE_WIDTH,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = POINT_SIZE,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = group_colours,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),

    breaks =
      scales::breaks_pretty(n = 4),

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.05)
    )
  ) +
  common_date_scale() +
  labs(
    x = "Date",
    y = "Species with detected\nrhodopsin protein",
    tag = "D"
  ) +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none"
  )


############################################################
# 17. COMBINE PANELS
############################################################

Rhodopsin_Environmental_Figure <- (

  (
    Environmental_Plot /
      Overall_RPF_Plot /
      Strategy_RPF_Plot /
      Contributor_Plot
  ) +

    plot_layout(
      heights = c(
        1.00,
        0.72,
        1.00,
        0.68
      ),

      guides = "collect"
    )

) &

  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )


############################################################
# 18. EXPORT FIGURE AND NUMERICAL DATA
############################################################

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    "SupplFig_Environmental_Rhodopsin_A4_Landscape.pdf"
  ),

  plot =
    Rhodopsin_Environmental_Figure,

  width = 11.69,
  height = 8.27,
  units = "in",
  device = cairo_pdf
)


ggsave(
  filename = file.path(
    "SupplFig_Environmental_Rhodopsin_A4_Landscape.png"
  ),

  plot =
    Rhodopsin_Environmental_Figure,

  width = 11.69,
  height = 8.27,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)


write_csv(
  environment_2_8m,
  file.path(
    "Environment_2_8m_Measured.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  overall_date_rpf,
  file.path(
    "Overall_Rhodopsin_Fraction.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  group_date_rpf,
  file.path(
    "Group_Rhodopsin_Fraction.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  species_date_rpf,
  file.path(
    "Species_Date_Rhodopsin_Fraction.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  rhodopsin_contributors,
  file.path(
    "Rhodopsin_Contributors_By_Date.csv"
  )
)

write_csv(
  rhodopsin_detected_species,
  file.path(
    "Rhodopsin_Detected_Species.csv"
  )
)


############################################################
# 19. QC AND CONSISTENCY CHECKS
############################################################

n_gene_carriers <- n_distinct(
  rhodopsin_gene_species$Species_ID
)

n_detected_species <- n_distinct(
  rhodopsin_detected_species$Species_ID
)


cat(
  "\n=== Whole-dataset rhodopsin checks ===\n"
)

cat(
  "Protein-table rows loaded:",
  nrow(protein_table),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Species-meta rows loaded:",
  nrow(species_meta),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Rhodopsin gene carriers:",
  n_gene_carriers,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Species with detected rhodopsin protein:",
  n_detected_species,
  "\n\n"
)


cat(
  "Detected rhodopsin species by Figure 5 group:\n"
)

print(
  rhodopsin_detected_species %>%
    count(
      Figure5_Group,
      name = "N_Rhodopsin_Species"
    )
)


cat(
  "\nMaximum detected simultaneously per group:\n"
)

print(
  rhodopsin_contributors %>%
    group_by(Figure5_Group) %>%
    summarise(
      Maximum_Detected = max(
        N_Rhodopsin_Species,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      .groups = "drop"
    )
)


# Panel B must equal the total-proteome-weighted average of
# the two group curves in panel C.
pooled_consistency <- group_date_rpf %>%
  group_by(Date) %>%
  summarise(
    Reconstructed_Overall_Percent =
      100 *
      sum(Rhodopsin_Abundance) /
      sum(Total_Protein_Abundance),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    overall_date_rpf %>%
      select(
        Date,
        Rhodopsin_Percent
      ),

    by = "Date"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Absolute_Difference =
      abs(
        Reconstructed_Overall_Percent -
          Rhodopsin_Percent
      )
  )


cat(
  "\nMaximum panel B/C reconstruction difference:",
  max(
    pooled_consistency$Absolute_Difference,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ),
  "\n"
)


if (n_detected_species != 47L) {
  warning(
    "Expected 47 rhodopsin-protein-positive species from Figure 5, ",
    "but detected ",
    n_detected_species,
    ". Inspect Rhodopsin_Detected_Species.csv and confirm that ",
    "the KO-only rule matches the manually curated Figure 5 ",
    "rhodopsin catalogue."
  )
}



Rhodopsin_Environmental_Figure
```

```{r}
############################################################
# EPILIMNETIC BACTERIAL ABUNDANCE VS TEMPERATURE
#
# INPUTS
# ------
# biotic_ST_dat:
#   date, bacteria
#   Bacterial abundance from the pooled 2–8 m sample.
#
# temperature_ST_profile:
#   date, depth, temperature
#   Interpolated temperature profile.
#
# MODELS
# ------
# 1. Pearson correlation:
#      bacterial abundance ~ mean 2–8 m temperature
#
# 2. Log-linear regression:
#      log(bacterial abundance) ~ mean 2–8 m temperature
#
# The log-linear temperature coefficient is converted to the
# percentage change in abundance per 1 °C.
#
# Only measured bacterial sampling dates are observations.
# No AR(1) correction is applied.
############################################################

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tibble)
})

ANALYSIS_START <- as.Date("2021-03-02")
ANALYSIS_END   <- as.Date("2021-06-04")

EPI_DEPTH_MIN <- 2
EPI_DEPTH_MAX <- 8


########################
## 1) Measured bacterial abundance
########################

bacteria_epilimnion <- biotic_ST_dat %>%
  transmute(
    Date = as.Date(date),
    Bacteria_Cells_Per_mL = as.numeric(bacteria)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    Date >= ANALYSIS_START,
    Date <= ANALYSIS_END,
    is.finite(Bacteria_Cells_Per_mL),
    Bacteria_Cells_Per_mL > 0
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date)


########################
## 2) Mean 2–8 m temperature
########################

temperature_epilimnion <- temperature_ST_profile %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(
    Date = as.Date(date),
    Depth_m = as.numeric(depth),
    Temperature_C = as.numeric(temperature)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    Date >= ANALYSIS_START,
    Date <= ANALYSIS_END,
    is.finite(Depth_m),
    is.finite(Temperature_C),
    Depth_m >= EPI_DEPTH_MIN,
    Depth_m <= EPI_DEPTH_MAX
  ) %>%
  semi_join(
    bacteria_epilimnion %>% select(Date),
    by = "Date"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Date) %>%
  summarise(
    Temperature_C = mean(Temperature_C),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


########################
## 3) Pair abundance and temperature
########################

bacteria_temperature <- bacteria_epilimnion %>%
  inner_join(
    temperature_epilimnion,
    by = "Date"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(Bacteria_Cells_Per_mL),
    is.finite(Temperature_C)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date)

if (nrow(bacteria_temperature) != 37L) {
  stop(
    "Expected 37 paired sampling dates, but found ",
    nrow(bacteria_temperature), "."
  )
}


########################
## 4) Abundance summary
########################

abundance_summary <- bacteria_epilimnion %>%
  summarise(
    N_Sampling_Dates =
      n(),

    Minimum_Cells_Per_mL =
      min(Bacteria_Cells_Per_mL),

    Minimum_Date =
      Date[which.min(Bacteria_Cells_Per_mL)][1],

    Maximum_Cells_Per_mL =
      max(Bacteria_Cells_Per_mL),

    Maximum_Date =
      Date[which.max(Bacteria_Cells_Per_mL)][1],

    Fold_Change =
      Maximum_Cells_Per_mL /
      Minimum_Cells_Per_mL
  )


########################
## 5) Pearson correlation
########################

pearson_test <- cor.test(
  bacteria_temperature$Bacteria_Cells_Per_mL,
  bacteria_temperature$Temperature_C,
  method = "pearson",
  alternative = "two.sided",
  conf.level = 0.95
)

pearson_summary <- tibble(
  N_Paired_Dates =
    nrow(bacteria_temperature),

  Pearson_r =
    unname(pearson_test$estimate),

  CI_95_Lower =
    unname(pearson_test$conf.int[1]),

  CI_95_Upper =
    unname(pearson_test$conf.int[2]),

  Test_Statistic_t =
    unname(pearson_test$statistic),

  Degrees_Of_Freedom =
    unname(pearson_test$parameter),

  P_Value =
    pearson_test$p.value
)


########################
## 6) Log-linear model
########################

temperature_model <- lm(
  log(Bacteria_Cells_Per_mL) ~ Temperature_C,
  data = bacteria_temperature
)

coefficient_table <- coef(
  summary(temperature_model)
)

coefficient_confidence <- confint(
  temperature_model,
  level = 0.95
)

model_parameters <- tibble(
  Term =
    rownames(coefficient_table),

  Estimate =
    coefficient_table[, "Estimate"],

  Standard_Error =
    coefficient_table[, "Std. Error"],

  Test_Statistic_t =
    coefficient_table[, "t value"],

  P_Value =
    coefficient_table[, "Pr(>|t|)"],

  CI_95_Lower =
    coefficient_confidence[, 1],

  CI_95_Upper =
    coefficient_confidence[, 2]
) %>%
  mutate(
    Percent_Change_Per_Degree_C =
      if_else(
        Term == "Temperature_C",
        100 * expm1(Estimate),
        NA_real_
      ),

    Percent_Change_CI_95_Lower =
      if_else(
        Term == "Temperature_C",
        100 * expm1(CI_95_Lower),
        NA_real_
      ),

    Percent_Change_CI_95_Upper =
      if_else(
        Term == "Temperature_C",
        100 * expm1(CI_95_Upper),
        NA_real_
      )
  )

model_fit <- summary(temperature_model)
model_f <- model_fit$fstatistic

model_summary <- tibble(
  Model =
    "lm(log(Bacterial abundance) ~ mean 2–8 m temperature)",

  N_Paired_Dates =
    nobs(temperature_model),

  R_Squared =
    model_fit$r.squared,

  Adjusted_R_Squared =
    model_fit$adj.r.squared,

  Residual_SD_Log_Scale =
    model_fit$sigma,

  Model_F =
    unname(model_f[1]),

  Numerator_DF =
    unname(model_f[2]),

  Denominator_DF =
    unname(model_f[3]),

  Model_P_Value =
    pf(
      model_f[1],
      model_f[2],
      model_f[3],
      lower.tail = FALSE
    )
)


########################
## 7) Print outputs
########################

print(
  abundance_summary,
  width = Inf
)

print(
  pearson_summary,
  width = Inf
)

print(
  model_parameters,
  width = Inf
)

print(
  model_summary,
  width = Inf
)
```
